title: Firmware Package Authenticity & Untrusted Origin Rejection
attack: Attacker uploads forged firmware signed by an untrusted or arbitrary self-signed key, attempting remote code execution.
observable: Ensure only authorized firmware images signed by a trusted certificate authority can be staged or installed.
defense: Root-of-Trust verification chain validating issuer signatures against on-device trust anchors stored in protected memory.
citations: Luo et al. (IEEE IoT 2022) Sec. V-C
notes: Requires hardware-backed public key in eFuse/ROM for absolute root-of-trust; software fallback validates against immutable keystore.

title: Payload Tampering & Cryptographic Hash Verification Failure
attack: Attacker modifies binary bytes (e.g. flipping privilege flags or patching jump addresses) during transport or in staging memory.
observable: Detect any unauthorized modification, corruption, or injection within the firmware binary.
defense: Cryptographic SHA-256 digest recalculation and comparison against the manifest hash prior to flash programming.
citations: Luo et al. (IEEE IoT 2022) Sec. V-C
notes: Hash checking is computationally bounded on 8-bit MCUs (ATmega328P); offloaded to hardware cryptoaccelerator on SAM L11 / ESP32.

title: Signature Validation Failure (Fanjas V3 Certificate 0 Model)
attack: Fault injection or algorithmic flaw bypasses certificate signature checking, accepting an invalid certificate 0.
observable: Reject packages where the cryptographic digital signature does not mathematically verify against the payload hash.
defense: Constant-time RSA/ECDSA signature verification with dual-check status enforcement and explicit error trapping.
citations: Fanjas et al. (DFT 2023) Sec. IV-A & V-B
notes: Pure software signature verification is vulnerable to precise clock/EM glitches unless implemented with complementary condition branches.

title: Replay of Stale Valid Update Request
attack: Attacker captures legitimate firmware update transmission and replays it over the network or bus at a later date.
observable: Prevent adversaries from re-transmitting previously authorized update payloads to induce state desynchronization.
defense: Monotonic transaction nonce and session-bound timestamp challenge verification on update start handshake.
citations: Luo et al. (IEEE IoT 2022) Table I
notes: Requires real-time clock or monotonically increasing state counter preserved across power loss.

title: Firmware Downgrade & Anti-Rollback Policy Enforcement
attack: Attacker downgrades device to an older legitimate firmware (v1.0.0) containing a known buffer overflow or logic bug.
observable: Prohibit the flashing of authentic, signed older firmware versions that contain known unpatched vulnerabilities.
defense: Anti-rollback enforcement comparing package version against a monotonic hardware counter in secure non-volatile memory.
citations: Luo et al. (IEEE IoT 2022) Sec. V-F & VII-B
notes: If hardware OTP fuses are exhausted, monotonic counter falls back to wear-leveled flash blocks protected by DAL/MPU.

title: Malformed / Incomplete Update Manifest & Header Parsing
attack: Attacker sends an image with corrupt magic bytes, negative chunk sizes, or out-of-bounds flash target offsets, crashing the bootloader.
observable: Ensure firmware parser is resilient against buffer overflows, invalid offsets, and integer underflows during header parsing.
defense: Strict length-bounded manifest validation and sanitization prior to allocating staging buffers or decoding fields.
citations: Luo et al. (IEEE IoT 2022) Sec. IV-B
notes: Parser must execute in unprivileged isolation or with strict memory bounds.

title: Unsupported Hardware Target / Architecture Mismatch
attack: Flashing AVR ATmega328P firmware onto an ESP32 or wrong pinout revision, causing pin contention or permanent hardware latch-up.
observable: Prevent accidental or malicious installation of firmware compiled for an incompatible target MCU or PCB revision.
defense: Mandatory hardware target ID and board revision compatibility checks encoded in signed manifest header.
citations: Luo et al. (IEEE IoT 2022) Sec. II-B
notes: Requires immutable PCB revision ID pin straps or factory-burned hardware IDs.

title: Interrupted / Truncated Chunked OTA Transfer
attack: Partial upload leaves flash in corrupted half-written state, bricking device on subsequent reboot.
observable: Maintain system availability when network drops or power failure interrupts firmware chunk reception mid-stream.
defense: Staging scratch buffer with transactional commit and dual-stage CRC verification; golden image remains active until final commit.
notes: Staging area requires either dedicated external SPI flash or dual internal flash partitions.

title: Unauthorized Update Requestor / Missing Transport Authentication
attack: Unauthenticated device on the local network or bus sends an OTA trigger command, staging malicious firmware.
observable: Restrict firmware update initiation endpoints strictly to authenticated operators and administrative consoles.
defense: Mutual TLS / bearer authorization token validation on the update initiation endpoint before accepting any chunks.
citations: Luo et al. (IEEE IoT 2022) Sec. III-E & V-A
notes: Microcontrollers acting as peripheral bus nodes require session challenge-response over UART/SPI.

title: Dual-Bank Safe Recovery & Inconsistent State Rollback
attack: Activated firmware passes static signature checks but enters bootloop or panic state upon executing hardware init.
observable: Guarantee automatic fallback to the known-good 'Golden' firmware bank if newly activated firmware crashes during boot.
defense: Dual-bank execution with hardware watchdog boot-grace timer; rollback to Bank A if Bank B fails to assert health status.
notes: Requires minimum flash capacity to store two full executable partitions.

title: Unexpected Target-State Corruption & Invariant Assertion
attack: Transient glitch flips register bits (e.g. state variable 0x00 -> 0x01), corrupting execution state without CPU trap.
observable: Detect register bit-flips and state corruptions caused by transient voltage or EM disturbances during execution.
defense: Software invariant assertions and redundant shadow state validation across critical execution milestones.
notes: Increases execution time by ~12-18% due to redundant state checks.

title: Instruction-Skip Behavior (F1/F2 Models)
attack: Single clock/voltage glitch causes CPU pipeline to fetch NOP or skip decrement instruction, altering loop counters.
observable: Prevent attackers from skipping critical instructions (decrement, sub, security check) via power/EM glitching.
defense: Dual-counter unrolled execution with cross-counter equality assertions (w0 == w1) and loop termination tripwires.
citations: Fanjas et al. (FDTC 2024) Algorithm 1 & Table I
notes: Hardware lockstep is only partially effective against EM glitches (Wiersma 2017 Table II); software dual-checks provide secondary defense.

title: Conditional Branch Hijacking (F3/F4 Models & Auth Bypass)
attack: Glitching the comparison instruction (cmp) or branch (beq/bne) causes execution of authenticated branch without credentials.
observable: Ensure conditional authentication branches cannot be forced into unauthorized execution paths by single-instruction skips.
defense: Complementary condition evaluation: checking `(flag == TARGET) && (flag_inv == ~TARGET)` with random delay jitter.
notes: A multi-glitch attack timed exactly across both complementary evaluations can theoretically succeed if delay is non-randomized.

title: Communication Bus Glitch & Frame Interruption
attack: Transient noise on UART/I2C/SPI lines flips bits or truncates packets, leading to malformed command execution.
observable: Prevent corrupted or interrupted bus frames from being processed as valid commands by the target.
defense: Framed packet protocol with preamble, length check, sequence index, payload CRC-16, and post-frame delimiter.
notes: Adds 4 bytes of overhead per serial frame.

title: Malformed, Duplicated, or Out-of-Order Telemetry
attack: Adversary captures and injects past command frames or bus reflection duplicates command triggers.
observable: Maintain deterministic ordering and reject duplicated or replayed commands across device telemetry channels.
defense: Sliding sequence window (size=64) tracking received sequence IDs; strictly rejecting duplicate or stale sequence numbers.
citations: Luo et al. (IEEE IoT 2022) Table I
notes: Window wraps after 2^32 packets; requires atomic sequence counter.

title: Watchdog Reset & Hang Containment
attack: Glitch vectors CPU into unmapped memory or invalid loop, causing persistent denial of service.
observable: Guarantee automatic reset and containment when CPU execution stalls or enters an infinite loop following a glitch.
defense: Independent hardware Watchdog Timer (WDT) serviced only after all subsystem invariant checks pass.
citations: Luo et al. (IEEE IoT 2022) Sec. VII-D-1
notes: Watchdog timeout period must exceed longest legitimate cryptographic computation.

title: Inconsistent Authorization State Transition
attack: A glitch during state assignment leaves the target in an ambiguous state where security controls are disabled prematurely.
observable: Ensure state transitions (e.g. UNVERIFIED -> AUTHORIZED) are atomic and resistant to mid-transition interruption.
defense: Two-phase commit state machine with transaction tokens and rollback on mid-flight exception.
citations: Luo et al. (IEEE IoT 2022) Sec. IV-B
notes: Requires atomic word writes in SRAM.

title: Missing Fault-Detection Events & Telemetry Gap Monitoring
attack: Attacker disconnects telemetry line or jams transceiver; backend remains oblivious to target compromise.
observable: Detect silent failure or bus jamming where telemetry ceases without an explicit crash notice.
defense: Continuous heartbeat monitoring with max-cadence threshold; missing 3 consecutive heartbeats escalates risk to HIGH.
notes: Requires background timer thread in backend monitoring bridge.

title: Unverified Recovery State & Post-Fault Quarantine
attack: After a fault triggers reset, target boots directly into operational mode while SRAM or registers retain corrupted data.
observable: Prevent compromised or glitch-corrupted targets from resuming normal operations without verifying integrity.
defense: Quarantine mode enforcement requiring comprehensive POST (Power-On Self-Test) diagnostic checks before releasing I/O.
notes: Quarantine state slightly extends boot duration (+45ms).

title: Failure to Fail Closed & Emergency Lockdown
attack: Software exception handler defaults to permissive return, allowing unauthorized memory dump or actuator activation.
observable: Guarantee that upon unhandled faults or persistent attack, target shuts down sensitive outputs rather than failing open.
defense: Fail-closed emergency shutdown: immediate zeroization of session keys, disabling transmitter drivers, and hardware latch.
notes: Requires manual power cycle or authenticated command to recover from hardware latch.

title: Unauthorized Hardware Configuration Changes (BOCOR/UROW Fuses)
attack: Malware running on device attempts to overwrite Non-Volatile Memory (NVM) configuration rows to disable security.
observable: Prevent unauthorized software from altering critical security fuses and boot configurations in silicon.
defense: Silicon fuse lock: BOCOR and UROW rows locked to DAL2 access privilege; changes rejected and require full chip erase.
citations: Luo et al. (IEEE IoT 2022) Sec. II-B & V-B
notes: Hardware specific to ARM Cortex-M23 (SAM L11); ATmega328P uses high-voltage fuse programming lockout.

title: Inadequate Device-Access Restriction (DAL Tiering)
attack: External debugger connects to SWD port and reads out sensitive firmware or cryptographic keys without credentials.
observable: Enforce strict Debugger Access Level (DAL) hierarchy to prevent unauthenticated memory dumping.
defense: Debugger Access Level 0 (DAL0) lockdown; transitioning to DAL1/DAL2 requires 128-bit Chip Erase Key (CEKEY).
citations: Luo et al. (IEEE IoT 2022) Sec. V-B & VII-B
notes: Level transition strictly executes ChipErase_ALL, ensuring secret assets are destroyed prior to debugger attachment.

title: SWD / JTAG Debug Port Exposure in Production
attack: Attacker physically probes JTAG/SWD test pads on PCB to gain interactive control of CPU execution.
observable: Permanently close or cryptographically protect debug interfaces on production units deployed in the field.
defense: Hardware JTAG disable fuse blown during factory provisioning; physical pin disconnect and DPA power profiling monitoring.
citations: Luo et al. (IEEE IoT 2022) Sec. III-A
notes: Wiersma et al. showed JTAG lock can be attacked via voltage/EM glitches; combining with fuse blow mitigates ROM timing bypass.

title: Flash Readback Protection Bypass & Lock Bit Tampering
attack: Attacker places MCU in parallel programming or ISP mode to dump proprietary IP and encryption keys.
observable: Prohibit external programmers from reading out internal flash memory contents across all programming modes.
defense: Flash Security Lock Bits (ATmega328P LB1=0, LB2=0) programmed to prohibit memory read commands via ISP.
notes: Can only be reset by full chip erase which wipes all flash and EEPROM contents.

title: Security Policy Misconfiguration (RXN / DXN Permissions)
attack: Attacker exploits stack buffer overflow to inject shellcode into SRAM and diverts PC to execute it.
observable: Prevent code execution from data RAM and data flash to defeat stack and heap buffer overflow code injection.
defense: Hardware Execute-Never policies: RAM Execute Never (RXN=1) and Data Flash Execute Never (DXN=1) in silicon fuses.
citations: Luo et al. (IEEE IoT 2022) Sec. V-D & VII-B (DXN/RXN)
notes: Defeats code injection; return-oriented programming (ROP) requires additional CFI / iASLR defenses.

title: Missing Boot-Time Device Integrity Verification
attack: Glitching during boot ROM execution causes skip of fuse verification, leaving device in unhardened default state.
observable: Verify hardware configuration integrity before allowing execution of application code.
defense: Hardware Boot ROM performs cryptographic digest check of BOCOR row and secure bootloader before passing execution.
citations: Luo et al. (IEEE IoT 2022) Sec. V-C
notes: Hardware boot ROM is immutable; must fail into halt loop if fuse digest mismatch is detected.

title: Anti-Rollback Enforcement Gaps in Silicon OTP Storage
attack: Software-managed version numbers in normal flash are wiped or restored to previous backups.
observable: Ensure version rollback protection cannot be cleared by power cycles or software manipulation.
defense: Hardware One-Time Programmable (OTP) monotonic fuse array; bits can only be burned (0->1) and never reversed.
citations: Luo et al. (IEEE IoT 2022) Sec. V-F
notes: Total counter updates bounded by physical OTP bit field size (e.g. 32 to 128 updates).

title: Insecure Provisioning & Illegal Lifecycle Transitions
attack: Attacker forces device back into Manufacturing or Unlocked lifecycle state to regain diagnostic privileges.
observable: Enforce unidirectional progression of device lifecycle (Manufacturing -> Provisioned -> Field Deployed -> Decommissioned).
defense: State machine locked by OTP silicon registers; irreversible state progression enforced by on-chip logic.
citations: Luo et al. (IEEE IoT 2022) Sec. III-A
notes: Decommissioning blows permanent security fuse, disabling all execution.

title: Failure to Detect Unauthorized Hardware State Transitions
attack: Attacker lowers supply voltage to 730mV or injects fast transients to induce timing errors (Fanjas 2024 Table II).
observable: Detect out-of-specification electrical conditions (under-voltage, clock glitch, extreme temperature) used in fault attacks.
defense: Internal Brown-Out Detector (BOD) and Clock Failure Detection (CFD) circuitry triggering immediate hardware reset.
citations: Fanjas et al. (FDTC 2024) Sec. IV-D & Table II
notes: BOD reaction time (~1-2us) is slower than nanosecond glitches; requires decoupling capacitor placement defense.

title: Inaccurate / Spoofed Lockdown Status Reporting
attack: Compromised target software reports 'LOCKED' status to backend while debug interface remains open.
observable: Ensure remote monitoring systems receive authentic, untampered proof of hardware lockdown status.
defense: Hardware attestation report signed by internal private key held in secure crypto-coprocessor (ATECC608A / TrustZone).
citations: Luo et al. (IEEE IoT 2022) Sec. V-A & VIII
notes: Requires asymmetric hardware key isolated from rich execution environment.

title: Weak Dataset Key Generation & Insufficient Entropy
attack: Pseudorandom generator initialized with predictable seed (e.g. boot time), allowing attacker to deduce secret keys.
observable: Guarantee that all cryptographic keys are generated using true physical entropy to prevent key predictability.
defense: Hardware True Random Number Generator (TRNG) / NIST SP 800-90A CSPRNG with continuous health tests.
citations: Luo et al. (IEEE IoT 2022) Sec. II-B
notes: TRNG entropy health tests must abort key generation if repetitive patterns are detected.

title: Unauthenticated Encryption & Nonce Reuse Vulnerability
attack: Reusing the same 96-bit Initialization Vector (IV) under AES-GCM allows mathematical recovery of authentication key and plaintext.
observable: Prevent keystream recovery and forgery in symmetric dataset encryption.
defense: Strict AES-256-GCM authenticated encryption with monotonic 96-bit nonce manager and historical collision cache.
citations: Luo et al. (IEEE IoT 2022) Sec. III-D
notes: Nonce cache bounds tracking to active session; persisted epoch counters prevent post-reboot collisions.

title: Ciphertext & Authentication Tag Tampering
attack: Bit-flipping in ciphertext or tag truncation bypasses data integrity checks, resulting in forged record processing.
observable: Detect any alteration to encrypted telemetry or stored records before attempting data processing.
defense: 128-bit GMAC authentication tag verification; immediate fail-stop upon tag mismatch before passing buffer to application.
citations: Luo et al. (IEEE IoT 2022) Sec. IV-B
notes: Decryption and authentication are performed in a single authenticated pass to avoid padding oracle attacks.

title: Unauthorized Sanitization Request / Missing Operator Privilege
attack: Malicious network actor invokes sanitization API, causing unauthorized permanent loss of operational logs.
observable: Prevent unauthorized entities from triggering data purge or key destruction commands.
defense: Cryptographically signed authorization token (dual-control operator signature) required for sanitization commands.
citations: Luo et al. (IEEE IoT 2022) Sec. III-A
notes: Requires root administrator public key installed during provisioning.

title: Key Rotation Failure & Key Wearout
attack: Using a single key across millions of messages increases side-channel leakage risk and vulnerability to cryptanalysis.
observable: Enforce proactive retirement of encryption keys before reaching cryptographic lifetime or invocation limits.
defense: Automated epoch-based key rotation; generation of Key V2, re-wrapping dataset headers, and retirement of Key V1.
notes: Existing stored datasets must either be re-encrypted or key version table retained in secure storage.

title: Key Revocation Enforcement & Immediate Access Revocation
attack: Device continues encrypting or decrypting with a key known to be compromised, leaking subsequent data.
observable: Ensure compromised or retired keys are instantaneously invalidated and barred from further cryptographic use.
defense: Real-time revocation list check inside the cryptographic engine; revoked keys return ACCESS_DENIED immediately.
citations: Luo et al. (IEEE IoT 2022) Sec. III-E
notes: Revocation status must be consulted before every encryption/decryption invocation.

title: Cross-Dataset Key Separation & Tenant Isolation
attack: Key assigned to Telemetry Dataset A is accidentally or maliciously used to decrypt Sensitive Config Dataset B.
observable: Enforce strict cryptographic boundaries between distinct datasets, tenants, and security domains.
defense: Cryptographic domain separation: dataset ID and tenant context bound into AES-GCM Additional Authenticated Data (AAD).
citations: Luo et al. (IEEE IoT 2022) Sec. V-A & VII-B
notes: Ensures cross-dataset ciphertext injection fails authentication tag verification even if keys are identical.

title: Dataset Deletion & Key Lifecycle Inconsistency
attack: File records are deleted from index but decryption key remains cached in RAM or flash, enabling forensic recovery.
observable: Ensure dataset deletion is atomic across index entries, memory buffers, and key-wrapping structures.
defense: Atomic purge lifecycle: synchronous deletion of directory references, memory zeroization, and key wrapping block destruction.
citations: Luo et al. (IEEE IoT 2022) Sec. IV-B
notes: Requires filesystem and key management coordination to prevent orphan keys.

title: Cryptographic Erasure (Crypto-Shredding) & Memory Zeroization
attack: Adversary seizes decommissioned or stolen device and extracts raw NAND/flash contents via chip-off forensics.
observable: Render encrypted target data permanently unrecoverable in milliseconds by destroying the master decryption key.
defense: Cryptographic erasure (NIST SP 800-88): secure multipass zeroization of master key in RAM and secure NVM, rendering ciphertext irreversibly unrecoverable.
citations: Luo et al. (IEEE IoT 2022) Sec. V-A
notes: Physical media cells retain ciphertext; security relies mathematically on 256-bit AES cipher strength.

title: Post-Erasure Recovery Attempts & Stale-Reference Handling
attack: Application attempts to read dangling dataset pointer after erasure, returning stale in-memory buffers or partial reads.
observable: Ensure all post-erasure read or recovery attempts strictly fail with documented error status and zero data leakage.
defense: Dangling handle trap: invalidating dataset handles, clearing read cache, and returning formal PERMANENTLY_PURGED status.
citations: Luo et al. (IEEE IoT 2022) Sec. IV-B
notes: Traps both API-level dereferencing and low-level cache buffers.
